translations.text: He bound him with iron chains that cannot be undone.
Nor did they merely leave him bound on the earth.
Rather, it is written that he threw him into the burning lake of fire—I mean, beneath the abyss and the darkness.
And so that you may understand the truth.
We too, my beloved, since we know how great is the joy of this feast spread before us today,
let us each adorn ourselves inwardly and outwardly, as we prepare to go to this great banquet today,
so that we may eat of the good things that Michael, the great warrior of the King of kings, has prepared for us.
But since it is a royal banquet,
we ought to wait until they invite
first those who hold high rank in the King's court, together with his great archangel Michael.
Afterward, we too may follow them. You have asked well, my beloved, for whoever humbles himself is exalted
and raised upright. But come, follow me, for look, the great ones
have already gone to Michael's banquet
and taken their places. Who are the great ones who took their places first?
Listen attentively.
Adam, Abel, and Seth his son;
Moses, Aaron, Joshua son of Nun, Gideon, Barak, Samson, and the kings David, Solomon, and Hezekiah;
Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, Daniel, the three holy ones, Elijah, and Elisha,
these great prophets; Zechariah and his son John, and the twelve apostles;
Stephen the archdeacon, the holy elder and priest Apa Simeon, the martyrs, and all the righteous.
Why am I speaking only of those on earth?
The Lord of glory is there, together with all the heavenly ranks: the angels and archangels, the principalities and authorities,
the cherubim and seraphim,
the thrones, dominions, and powers. They are there,
all of them, giving glory to God and his great holy archangel Michael.
But I want to return once more to the court of the archangel Michael,
to these great men of the earth, and ask
about this great feast spread out today,
so that I too may rejoice with those who rejoice, according to the words of the teacher Paul the apostle.
However, I will begin first
with the father of all humanity,
whom God formed in his likeness and image. For he is the one I see occupying the first place
among those reclining at today's feast, and I will ask him.
But will I dare to speak to him? For I am afraid.
and I tremble.
Look, now I also see everyone at today's banquet giving him glory
and honoring him. I too will count myself among them,
even though I am a sinner.
I will offer him a joyful greeting with my tongue, like this: “Greetings, my holy father!
Lord, greetings, father of all my fathers and of all humanity yet to come!”
When I offer him this threefold joyful greeting befitting his glory,
he will certainly call out in turn, like a father to his son: “Come, you too, and rejoice with us at the great feast spread out for us today.” Once I have gained the freedom to speak in his presence,
I will ask him: “My lord and father, are you not the one whom God formed with his own hands?
He filled you with the glory of his likeness and image.
Are you not the one about whom God commanded all the heavenly ranks, saying, ‘Come and worship the work of my hands, my likeness and my image’?”
Adam answered: “Yes, my son, I am
the one to whom all these things happened.” I will answer him again: “My lord and father, did not all these things happen, and did not all the angels bow down to you, except
one alone and his rank?”
He answered: “Yes, my Lord made everything submit to me before I was placed in paradise.”
I will dare to say
to him: “What have you to do with today's feast, since no angel is greater than you? You are the likeness and image of God.”
But Adam said, “Listen to me, my son.
I will tell you about the honor of today's feast, because I understand more than you do.
And I was there when all these things were going to happen, at the time when my Lord
And my God,
and my Creator made me according to his likeness and his image.
He adorned me beautifully.
He breathed a breath of life into my face.
He seated me on a throne of glory before him.
He commanded all the orders of heaven by his true authority, saying, ‘Come and worship the work of my hands, my likeness and my image.’ Mastema was also there, being the first-created being.
He is the one now called the devil, and he was an archangel.
Then, when the command came from the Father's mouth,
Michael came, one of the seven angels,
with his whole order, and they worshiped God our King.
Afterward they worshiped me too, saying, ‘We worship you, God the Creator,
and we worship the one you created according to your likeness and your image.’
Afterward Gabriel came with his whole order, and they too worshiped me, just as Michael had.
Likewise, all the heavenly hosts did so, according to their order and their ranks.
Last of all, the Master said to Mastema, which means ‘hatred,’ ‘You too, come and worship the work of my hands, my likeness and my image, just like all your companions.’
Satanael answered angrily and said to the Lord, ‘If there is no rank beneath you higher than I am, except for me alone,
and I come after you in glory because I am the first-created being, am I now to come and worship dust?
May it never happen to me that I should worship this one! Rather, he must worship me, because I existed before him.’
The Merciful One said, ‘Satanael, listen to me. I am your God. I am your Creator. Come now and worship the work of my hands.’
Mastema said, ‘May it never happen to me!
Neither I
nor my whole legion will worship someone inferior to us.
For we are spirits, but this one is dust. I will not worship him.’
He said to him again, a second and a third time, “My first-formed creature, was it not I who appointed you commander-in-chief under me and made my angels submit to you?
Are you now going to rebel against my kingdom?
Are you now going to display disobedience that will endure forever?
Are you now going to teach slaves to rise up against their masters?
Are you now going to signal disobedience, Mastema? Are you not my slave? Am I not your master?
Do I not have the authority to cast you out of my presence and take my great glory away from you,
which now has no equal in my entire kingdom,
except for me, my Father, and the Holy Spirit? Obey me and bow down to the creature I have formed.”
The boastful, envious one said before the one to whom everything submits, “It will never happen that I and my entire order bow down to two masters.
Moreover, there is no one [?] greater than I except you in the entire kingdom of heaven.
And if I wish, I and my order will suffice for my entire kingdom on our own.
It will never happen that I bow down to someone lesser than I.”
Immediately God, who is free from anger, became angry.
He gave an order to a great cherub, who struck him and weakened him.
He commanded Michael, who stripped him of his belt and breastplate,
along with his staff of light and his sapphire headdress.
He took all his glory away from him and gave him a dark appearance, together with all those who were with him, and cast him out of his kingdom.
Michael did everything he had been commanded to do.
He seized Satan, stripped him of his power, and cast him out of heaven along with all those who were with him. He cast him out of his kingdom.
The good God called Michael when he saw his zeal for the creature he had formed,
and his willingness to fight for his Lord.
He said to him in the midst of all his heavenly orders, “Michael”—which means “power,” while “El” means “God”—“come,” he said, “my holy steward Michael.
Come, you who fought and conquered! Come to me, Michael, you who carry out your king’s command.
Look, I have recognized your goodwill toward me and all that I have formed.
I, in turn, will direct my goodwill toward you.”
Open your mouth, Michael, and receive all my mercies within you.
So that you may continue pleading with me at all times on behalf of my likeness and my image.
And I, in turn, will forgive them.
For I know that Mastema will contend with my creation, wanting me to cast them away from me, just as I cast him out of my kingdom.
But look, I have entrusted you with my creation so that you may save them from his snares.
And plead with me on their behalf.
If they sin, I will forgive them, for I am a merciful God.
Look, Michael, today I appoint you over all the ranks of my kingdom.
And apart from me, my Father, and the Holy Spirit, there is no one greater than you among all the ranks of heaven.
Archangel Michael, come and stand at my right hand. Remain close to my throne at all times, commanding all the powers of heaven, who will obey you in everything.
Michael, you are the one who will teach all the ranks to serve me uprightly. Michael, you are the pride
and the knowledge of my kingdom.
Raise your head, which you lowered
when you bowed down before my creation, and I will place upon it this great glory that I took away from the arrogant one.
Stretch out your hand and take this staff of light.
Become commander-in-chief in place of the disgraced commander-in-chief. Michael, stretch out your hand and take this staff, and become commander-in-chief in place of the accuser
who was disgraced. Michael, stretch out your left hand
and take this great weapon, and prepare yourself to fight the enemies of your king.
Michael, take the sapphire belt and fasten it around your waist,
so that those who oppose your Lord will see you and immediately be dismayed.
Open your mouth, my minister.
Receive power,
so that your speech will be like the sound of a multitude speaking.
Come, Michael, and wear my glory.
So that you will teach everyone to give me glory.
Look, I have understood your entire desire toward my creation.
Come now and serve me throughout the whole life of my image.
Look at Adam now: you see him there alone, with no one else corresponding to him.
But look, I have placed a sign in his rib, which will come into being from him.
For I have already said, Michael, that it is not good for the man to remain alone.
Instead, let us make him a helper corresponding to him. Michael, Adam’s helper is one with him,
from the moment I formed him.
But I have not yet brought her to him. Michael, if I had made Adam to remain alone,
there would have been no need for me to plant a paradise either, Michael,
the archangel. This whole world beneath my throne—
I will cause it to be populated in the likeness of Adam, who is my image. But now, Michael,
look, I have appointed you steward over my kingdom, so that you may serve with compassion.
toward the creature I formed.
Michael, Adam’s descendants will know my name through you.
Michael, you are the commander-in-chief of the heavenly host. Michael, ruler of those in heaven and those on earth! Michael, you are the incense burner at the time of my holy sacrifice.
Michael, you are the one who will present my offering to me on behalf of Adam’s descendants.
Great deeds will be done by Adam’s children. You, Michael, are the one who will plead on their behalf so that I may forgive them.
The children of Adam’s line will blaspheme against me through the one who leads them astray.
But I will forgive them through your pleas, Michael.
When the Lord had said all these things to Michael,
he stretched out his hand.
He placed the crown on him and made him an archangel.
He placed three seals upon him in the form of the Holy Trinity, with the likeness of his image upon the seals,
so that the archangel would continually plead with God on behalf of his image. That, indeed, is why I have come to this feast, Michael’s banquet today. I am Adam, your father.
Abel, innocent young son, I beg you: you too, tell me about your joy today at Michael’s feast.
“I rejoice,” he said, “because the one whose feast you celebrate today is the one who pleaded with God for my father and my mother until they were forgiven for the transgression they had committed.
And he is the one who carried my gifts up to God until he accepted my sacrifices from me.”
He paid no attention to what my brother offered, because he had not brought it with uprightness. That is why I rejoice today.
“Seth, I see you celebrating today at the feast of the holy archangel Michael.” “I am celebrating,” he said, “because when Cain killed my brother Abel,
God gave me to my parents.
And my mother could find no milk to nurse me,
because she had wasted away from grief over my brother Abel.
But the archangel Michael himself provided me with my spiritual nourishment from heaven.
That is why I rejoice today.”
“O righteous Enoch, whom God took away,
why are you too rejoicing at this feast today?” “I am rejoicing,” he said,
“because I am the one who writes down the sins
and the good deeds of the whole world with my own hands.
Michael, the holy archangel, is the one who brings them before God. He presents the good deeds to him; as for the sins, he pleads with God on their behalf until he has mercy and forgives them.
That is why I rejoice today.”
“Methuselah, righteous old man,
who advanced well in years,
what is the reason for your joy today? For I see you looking radiant [?] in the midst of this banquet today.”
He said, “Why should I not rejoice? I am the eighth from Adam.
The archangel Michael brought my prayer up to God,
and he granted me a long life,
so that my lifespan and my years surpassed those of my father Adam: nine hundred and thirty-nine years.
That is why I rejoice today.”
“O righteous Noah, are you rejoicing today at the feast of the archangel Michael?”
“How could I not rejoice?
For when God became angry and was going to destroy the world, he brought me into an ark with my wife, my children, and all the creatures that move upon the earth.
He shut the door of the ark behind us, and the floodgates of heaven and earth opened and surrounded us.
For forty days and forty nights we did not see the sun.
nor the moon, nor a star.
But Michael, the holy archangel, guided us and the ark.
He kept pleading with God until the water subsided and dry land appeared, so that I and those with me could be saved.
That is why I rejoice today.
“Abraham the patriarch, are you too rejoicing today at the feast of the holy archangel Michael?” “Yes,” he said, “I rejoice today,
because I am the first person whom Michael visited,
together with my Lord and his other companion, the archangel Gabriel.
And Michael pleaded with God on my behalf, and he gave me Isaac, my son.
And if indeed I am worthy,
I ate with him under the tree at Mamre. That is why I rejoice today.” “O righteous one,
Isaac, the holy promise,
and holy sacrifice acceptable to the living God,
why are you too so splendidly dressed at the feast of the holy archangel Michael?” “I am dressing for the celebration,” he said, “because I am the only child of my father and mother.
They have no child besides me, nor will they have another after me.
My father bound my hands and feet.
He placed me on stones on a deserted mountain.
With my own eyes I saw the knife in my father's hand as he was about to slaughter me.
The archangel Michael provided a sheep in my place.
He seized the knife in my father's hand as he was about to slaughter me.
My sacrifice was completed. That is why I rejoice today.”
“Jacob the patriarch, who prevailed with God,
and are mighty among men, are you too rejoicing today?”
“Yes,” he said, “I rejoice today.
For when my brother Esau pursued me to kill me, I went up to Mesopotamia in Syria, to Laban.
Michael was the one who came to me and set apart my wages for me from the livestock. He blessed me,
my children, and my wives. That is why Israel took its name from me.”
That is why I rejoice today.
O Joseph, righteous and wise, whom they envied, why are you too rejoicing today?
Joseph said, “Truly, I have reason to rejoice today, because when my brothers envied me, they sold me into a foreign land.
I became poor and miserable, with no one to help me, in great distress.
The archangel came to me, rescued me, and made me a king.
That is why I rejoice today.”
Moses, Aaron, and Joshua son of Nun,
what about you too, today at this great celebration, at the feast of the archangel Michael?
The holy ones said, “The joy is indeed ours, because Michael is the one who traveled with us and his people.
He also destroyed our enemies and led the way
before us into the promised land.
That is indeed why we rejoice today.”
Gideon, I see you too rejoicing today at Michael’s banquet.
“I rejoice greatly,” he said, “because Michael is the one who came to me.
He filled me with his power, and I went and struck down Midian [?].
The people were saved. That is why I rejoice today.”
O Manoah and Anna his wife,
how great is your joy today? The judges said, “Truly, we rejoice today, because
we had been childless since our youth; no child had been born to us.
We continued praying and offering sacrifices to God so that we would be remembered, and God gave us Samson the mighty.
Our other son too rejoices with us today.”
David, the father of Christ according to the flesh,
and joyful king, I see you today playing your ten-stringed lyre at Michael’s banquet.
David said, “Yes, I rejoice today,
and I dress in finery,
because the [?] of all the Lord’s feasts
and his ministers, written on the tablets of my heart.
And this too is fitting for today's feast: “The angel of the Lord encamps around those who fear him
and rescues them.” That is why I rejoice today.
“Wise Solomon, are you too rejoicing today?” “Yes,” he said, “I rejoice,
because Michael, who has stood beside me since my childhood, brought peace in my days.
And he carried my prayer up to God, and I built his house. That is why I rejoice today.”
“Hezekiah, righteous king, do you not rejoice today at the feast of the archangel Michael?”
“Yes,” he said, “I rejoice today,
because when the Assyrians surrounded me and my people, it was Michael the archangel who went and struck them down at night.
They numbered a hundred and eighty-five thousand men. My people and I were saved. That is why I rejoice today.”
“O Isaiah, great prophet,
what is your joy today, you too,
at Michael's feast?” “This is my joy,” he said: “All these blows they inflicted on me, and these insults,
at the hands of King Manasseh and those with him—
it was Michael the archangel who stood beside me.
He gave me strength until they sawed me through the middle
with a wooden saw. That is why I rejoice today.”
“My holy father Jeremiah,
I see you today with your great shining lamp, rejoicing at the feast of the archangel Michael.”
“I rejoice greatly,” he said, “because after I had spent seven years in captivity
with my people, the holy archangel Michael
pleaded with the one who lives forever, and he put mercy into the hearts of the Babylonian kings.
They released us, and we returned to Jerusalem.
That is why I rejoice today.”
“Ezekiel the prophet, come and tell us why you are leaping for joy today.”
“At the feast of the holy archangel Michael, I leap with confidence,” he said,
“and I rejoice because Michael the archangel
brought me a scroll. He gave me a command, and I ate it.
The prophecies were revealed to me.
That is why I rejoice today.”
“Hananiah, Azariah, Mishael,
are you rejoicing today
at the feast of the holy archangel Michael?”
“Yes,” said the three holy saints.
“We rejoice and are glad, because the one whose feast you celebrate today is the one who came into the middle of the blazing, fiery furnace.
He extinguished it for us.
He made the king believe in God.
Our martyrdom was brought to completion.
That is why we rejoice today.” “Daniel, beloved man,
are you too rejoicing today at this great feast?
I think you rejoice even more.” Daniel said, “What other joy can equal my joy?
For it was not just once,
or twice, that I saw Michael, the true ruler.
And when I was thrown into the lions’ den,
it was Michael, the commander-in-chief, who came to me and shut the lions’ mouths.
That is why I rejoice today.”
“You twelve apostles, are you rejoicing today at this great feast?” “We rejoice,” they said, “because after this great sorrow that came upon us
when they crucified our Lord Jesus Christ,
while we were hiding for fear of the Jews, Mary the virgin came and told us, ‘I went with those who were with me to see the tomb early on Sunday.
We found the holy archangel Michael.’
He rolled away the stone and sat down on it.
And he gave us the good news that the Lord had risen.
That is why I rejoice today.
Saint Zechariah the priest and John his son.
They too rejoice at the feast of the holy archangel Michael.
“Yes,” the saints said, “we rejoice,
because he appointed the archangel as his commander-in-chief.
I myself serve him as a priest, and my son John is the son of Elizabeth, the relative of Mary, the mother of Jesus, my relative by human descent.
That is why we rejoice today.”
Stephen, the chief deacon
and first martyr, do you too rejoice today at the feast of Michael the archangel?
“Yes,” he said, “my joy is great,
“Because, at the time when they stoned me,
I lifted my eyes and saw the heavens opened. I saw the archangel Michael and all his angels pleading on my behalf.
And I saw Jesus standing at the right hand of the Father.
That is why I rejoice today.”
All the martyrs and the righteous,
do you rejoice today at Michael’s feast?
“Yes,” the saints said, “we truly rejoice today,
because, in every affliction that overtook us and every torture inflicted on us,
it was the archangel Michael who gave us strength, and we endured them until we completed our struggle and received honors.
That is why we rejoice today.”
All the heavenly orders also rejoice with us today at the feast of the holy archangel Michael. “Yes,” they said, “all the joy is indeed ours, from the time
when the Creator overthrew the proud one and appointed the humble one over us, the great holy archangel Michael. That is why we rejoice today.”
Truly, my beloved, great is the honor of today’s feast, which is spread out for us not only on earth but also in heaven. Now then, you listeners who love learning,

let us too make every effort to be found at Michael’s feast, so that we too may eat from the abundance of good things set before us for our benefit, together with all the saints whose names we have mentioned.
Perhaps, my beloved, we might dare to go to the commander-in-chief’s banquet without being properly dressed.
Instead, we might go in dirty clothes, with our bodies also covered in filth, and you would find us standing in shame among the well-dressed guests, who pull their robes close around themselves.
They wave us away, lest we come close to them and they become defiled by us.

And after regarding us with such suspicion, they will throw us out. For these are certainly the words that those who are properly dressed will say to us: “You foolish people! Are you not ashamed to be like this?
And even if you are not ashamed, do you not fear the true king, Jesus Christ, and his holy archangel Michael? Do you not know whose court this is?
and whose banquet this is?”
Does it not belong to the king and his holy archangel Michael, the commander-in-chief who excels in battle before his Lord, who gives him all these honors because of his strength?
I am truly amazed at you! What gave you the confidence to enter the inner court,
especially with your limbs exposed?
Have you not heard him saying, ‘Do not enter
my wedding hall without wearing wedding clothes’?
Or have you not heard him speak about the man who dared
to enter in dirty clothes like yours?
Do you understand what happened to him?
It is written that he had him bound hand and foot and threw him into the outer darkness. There will be weeping there
and gnashing of teeth.
Now then, brothers, withdraw to the outer court, a little way from the door,
so that when our Lord the king enters with his great holy archangel, you may plead with him. Perhaps he will give you a little relief,
along with the rest of those who beg for charity at the court’s entrance. For the archangel whose festival you are celebrating is merciful.
He will not leave you with nothing. But save yourselves!
Do not let them find you in this filth in the midst
of today’s festival, lest we share in the suffering of the others.”
Look, I have told you, and you have heard, my beloved, the rebukes that these people had to endure,
especially since those speaking to them are human beings like themselves,
and not God. But perhaps someone will say to me, “What are these dirty clothes, or what are these stains on the body?
Is there favoritism with God? Or does God love the rich person more than the poor? Is it that I myself do not want to dress well?”
Does anyone want to be disgraced?
No, that is not how it is, my dear one.
Let us never say that God shows favoritism, loving the rich more than the poor.
But listen, and I will tell you about the good offering and the worthless one. When you come to Michael’s banquet, anoint your head, wash your face, and cast hypocrisy away from you.
And you will do well.
If you are invited to Michael’s banquet, cleanse your heart of every kind of malice and slander, and your clothing will be radiant.
And you will celebrate the feast properly.
When you enter the church of God, which is Michael’s house,
strip yourself of sexual immorality, every passion, and every defilement.
Clothe yourself in peace, purity, and righteousness.
And you will enter the court with joy and celebrate with the holy archangel Michael. If you are invited to the wedding feast of the king and his great commander,
let your acts of mercy and love open the door of the wedding hall for you.
And whatever you give, you will find repaid tenfold on your table before you.
If you wish to honor Michael, the king’s commander-in-chief,
let widows and orphans leave your presence with joyful faces and their bodies clothed, according to your means.
And I tell you that your gift will be great in the sight of God and the archangel Michael. If you wish to go joyfully to Michael’s banquet, then welcome strangers into your home
at Michael’s feast, and enjoy yourself with them.
And Michael will come out joyfully and bring you into his king’s court in peace.
If someone pleads with you, asking you for anything in Michael’s name, do not hesitate to give it to him.
I tell you, my dear one, that whatever you give to that person,
Michael himself will take it in his hands and offer it on God’s day on your behalf.
And he will repay these things to you with interest on earth.
And God will have mercy on you in his kingdom, for it is written, “Mercy triumphs over judgment.”
And also, “Show mercy, so that mercy may be shown to you.”
If you persist in celebrating the feast of the archangel Michael once each month, that is, on the twelfth day,
on the day of his appointment, and keep taking care of his offering and providing service according to your ability. He will continue
—the archangel Michael himself—to plead with God for you at all times, so that he may grant you everything you need, beyond what you imagine.
But perhaps, my dear friend, you will say to me, “If I give charitable gifts and offerings, I will give them to God.
Is Michael a god, that I should offer my sacrifice to him? There is no god besides the God of heaven, the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.”
I, in turn, will answer you, “Well said, believer! Truly, your faith is directed rightly toward your Lord.
But listen, and let me explain to you—to everyone.
Is it not one king who rules over the lands, with many ranks of officials under him?
Among these ranks you will find one higher than another, while the king is higher than them all.
Now, suppose someone forms a friendship
with someone in these royal ranks and gives him honors and money.
Does he give these to him as part of the rank he holds?
No, rather, he gives them to him knowing that his rank is great,
and that he is close to the king at all times,
and that he can rescue him from every dangerous situation, also recommending him to the king
as a useful person,

so that others too may receive favor through him. This is also how it is with everyone who gives charitable gifts and offerings to God on Michael’s day: the archangel receives their sacrifices from them
and their charitable gifts, and presents them to God like a great, sweet fragrance. He receives a command from God concerning them and prepares many good things for them.
He also obtains favor for them before God, so that they may be free from punishment forever.
But if you want to know that the things people give as charitable gifts
and offerings to God on the day
of the holy archangel Michael, he administers for them while they are still in the world,
listen to this great and wonderful account, to the glory of God and his holy archangel Michael.
There was a righteous man who loved God and loved giving charitable gifts. He lived in the border regions and had a wise wife
who was also modest.
She too was perfect in compassion and love, just like her husband.
These people had great devotion to the archangel Michael.
The man's name was Dorotheus, and his wife's name was Theopiste.
From the time they were married to one another, while both were young,
they possessed a well-established estate that they had inherited from their parents.
They owned many animals and considerable wealth to meet the needs of life in this world.
These holy people, Dorotheus and his wife Theopiste, had a custom honoring the holy archangel Michael whenever the twelfth day of each month arrived.
They would prepare the offering on the eleventh, and early the next morning, on the twelfth, they would joyfully send the firstfruits and the offering to the archangel's sanctuary.
Afterward, they would slaughter a sheep and prepare pots of meat
and vegetables, and bake enough bread for their needs.
After receiving the holy mysteries, they would invite every needy person they could find, along with the blind and the lame,
the widows, the orphans, and the strangers,
and anyone else they could find. They would bring them into their home, and the two of them would stand beside them and serve them until they had finished eating.
They would also give them plenty of wine.
When they saw that they were about to leave, they would anoint their heads with oil and send them off joyfully, saying, “Go in peace, beloved brothers and sisters.
For we have been found worthy of a great blessing:
you have come to us today.”
They did these things on every twelfth day, so that their sweet fragrance and their love rose to God in heaven.
Everyone honored them throughout their lives because of their excellence.
Yet they concealed their virtue and sought no human honor at all.
Instead, all their hope rested in God
and the archangel Michael.
After they had continued in this way for a long time, God gave a command.
The flood came without the water spreading over the land, as a punishment for human beings because of their sins.
He then held it back for three consecutive years,
so that the land of Egypt fell into great turmoil.
and those upon it, and they would forget the abundance in Egypt, as it is written.
Then many people and animals died,
because the water had not flooded the land for three consecutive years. But the holy man
and his wife did not stop what they did every month, pleading with God and the holy archangel Michael,
“Do not let your charitable feast and your offering fail in our hands, we who are your servants.” While they continued like this,
they too began to suffer shortages, and many of their animals died. In short,
they completed two years.
and began the third.
